nodes.label: The flood-sheet PDFs
nodes.detail: data/raw/floodmaps/*.pdf, the city's sheets as downloaded. Read with pdftotext on 2026-09-11, the first line of every sheet titles it a flood map (Oversvømmelseskort) for its catchment at a hundred-year event in 2010.

nodes.label: The works layers
nodes.detail: In data/raw: skp_bassiner_pladser_kk, skp_veje_tunneller_kk and skp_terraenaend, titled 'Skybrudsplan' layers in data/raw/_manifest.json, and skp_igangsatte_prj_kk and skp_afsluttede_prj_kk, titled climate adaptation projects in progress (igangsatte) and completed (afsluttede); floodgap.py counts these last as built or started.

nodes.label: The sheet placements
nodes.detail: data/derived/floodmaps/_georef.json: each sheet's placement and its `confident` flag; floodgap.py places only flagged sheets and lists any other as missing.

nodes.label: The plan register

nodes.label: Rain-dependent discharge points
nodes.detail: data/raw/vp3_basis_2019_punkt_rbu_udl.geojson: points with structure type (`bgv_type`), municipality and basin volume (`vol_sb`), as fetched and clipped by municipality.

nodes.label: Treatment-plant discharge points

nodes.label: Structure-type codes
nodes.detail: data/manual/codelists.json: each structure-type code with its Danish name from the data instruction for rain-dependent outlets, and this project's English.

nodes.label: Curated structures

nodes.label: Plan pages on the tunnel
nodes.detail: data/raw/plan_projects.json, the pages 'Arealreservation Kalvebod Brygge Skybrudstunnel' (`K1.57`), 'Supplement Kalvebod Brygge Skybrudstunnel' and 'Supplement til VEL45 Kalvebod Brygge Skybrudstunnel': the tunnel drains a large catchment to Inderhavnen; the reservation page provides for deep shafts; the first supplement says the shaft at Skt. nodes.label: report.py
nodes.detail: Renders the register page; splits each joined map value into its ids and looks each up among the ids the plan cites; renders a curated note only under a registered claim.

saw.said on ARCHIVE.md: The bottom half attenuates less, and the gap closes the deeper the profile begins. That ordering is the whole result. It runs opposite to resuspension — a turbid layer over the bed would make the bottom half steeper, and it does so in only 22–48% of casts, outweighed on average by something else. The something else is that a PAR sensor counts photons across the whole band without distinguishing them, and water absorbs the band unevenly - as an earlier version of this page put it, roughly 0.5 per metre at 700 nm against 0.015 per metre at 450 nm. The red part of the light is gone near the surface, and what continues downward is the fraction water attenuates least. So the apparent broadband Kd falls with depth in perfectly uniform water, purely because the surviving spectrum has shifted. If that is the mechanism, the effect must fade for profiles that begin below the red-absorbing layer, because the red is already gone. It does: the ratio runs from 0.879 for profiles starting at the surface to 0.987 for those starting below 5.1 m, rising overall though not at every step.
